title: The Summer of the Old Mill House
premise: Paloma Eriksen inherited the Old Mill House vineyard along with its crushing debts, and she has spent ten years keeping her heart as carefully pruned as her vines. When her family reunion threatens to expose how far the estate has fallen, she hires Theo Marchetti, a quiet carpenter restoring the mill, to pose as her boyfriend for one weekend. The fake date turns devastatingly real, but Theo is hiding a decade-old secret: he was the boy Paloma loved and lost the summer before everything burned, and he has returned carrying a rehearsed confession about the fire that nearly destroyed them both. As creditors circle and the truth of that long-ago night surfaces, Paloma must decide whether survival means selling the mill house or finally trusting the man who came back to pay a debt of his own.
about_author: Tamsin Coldharbour spent her twenties working harvest seasons in forgotten wine regions, collecting stories from people who stayed when everyone else left. She writes romances about second chances, ruined houses, and the stubborn arithmetic of love versus debt.

chapters.title: The Ledger and the Vine
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. Opening at dawn in the vineyard, Paloma reviews the vineyard's accounts: three payments behind, the bank's final notice pinned under a wine glass. Her sister calls to confirm the family reunion at the Old Mill House in two weeks. Beat: weary defiance masking dread.

chapters.title: A Carpenter's Hands
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Theo arrives to repair the mill's sagging porch, hired on a neighbor's recommendation. He recognizes Paloma instantly; she doesn't recognize him. He takes the job anyway, telling himself ten years is long enough for anything. Beat: guilt disguised as coincidence.

chapters.title: Terms of Engagement
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. Cornered by her mother's phone call — bring someone or admit failure — Paloma impulsively offers Theo double wages to play her boyfriend for the reunion weekend. He hesitates, then agrees too quickly. Beat: a bargain both parties suspect they'll regret.

chapters.title: Rehearsal for a Lie
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Over wine on the mill porch, they invent their history: how they met, first date, his work. The invented details keep colliding with real memories Theo can't explain knowing. Beat: intimacy growing inside a lie.

chapters.title: The Family Arrives
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. Cars crunch up the gravel drive: her imperious aunt Margit, her brother Anders with his perfect marriage, cousins who measure worth in hectares. Theo performs charmingly well — too well, answering questions before they're asked. Beat: performance shading into truth.

chapters.title: Dessert and Damage
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. At the reunion dinner, Aunt Margit announces the family will buy the failing vineyard out from under Paloma 'for her own good.' Theo, furious, defends her with a passion no hired boyfriend should have. Under the table, Paloma takes his hand. Beat: the fake becomes real by dessert.

chapters.title: What the Fire Took
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. Alone after the guests sleep, Paloma tells Theo about the summer she was nineteen: the harvest festival, a boy named Teo who vanished the night the old barn burned, and the accusation that followed her family. Theo goes very still. Beat: the past knocking.

chapters.title: Ten Years of Sentences
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Theo privately rehearses the confession he has carried since he fled: he saw what started the fire, and staying silent protected the wrong person. His lawyer's letter in his jacket gives him until month's end to testify. Beat: time running out.

chapters.title: Margit's Offer
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. Aunt Margit corners Paloma with a private deal: sign over the mill house and the family will quietly erase the debts — and bury an old rumor about the fire. Paloma realizes the reunion was never about concern. Beat: power revealing its corruption.

chapters.title: Rain on the Mill Roof
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. A storm traps Theo and Paloma in the mill while repairing shutters. Wet, laughing, close, they almost kiss — and Theo pulls back, saying 'You don't know who I am.' Paloma demands answers; he promises them, just not yet. Beat: longing against secrecy.

chapters.title: The Neighbor's Testimony
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Theo visits old Henrik, the only other witness to the night of the fire, now dying. Henrik confirms what Theo saw: it was young Anders, drunk, knocking over lanterns — and Margit paid to make it disappear. Beat: the secret gaining weight.

chapters.title: Anders Smiles
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. Anders lingers after the reunion weekend, probing about Theo, oddly hostile. He warns Paloma that her carpenter 'isn't what he seems' — and his fear looks less like suspicion than recognition. Beat: threat closing in from within the family.

chapters.title: The Bank's Deadline
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. The bank rejects Paloma's restructuring plea; thirty days to pay or auction. Margit's offer now looks like rescue. Paloma, exhausted, starts drafting the transfer papers — then stops at the clause requiring her to sell the mill itself. Beat: survival priced in memory.

chapters.title: Confession, Interrupted
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. On the mill bridge at dusk, Theo finally begins: 'The summer of the fire, I—' A car horn, then Anders arriving unannounced, cuts him off. Anders and Theo lock eyes with mutual recognition. Beat: the sentence half-spoken, tension doubled.

chapters.title: Blackmail in the Barrel Room
chapters.summary: Anders' POV (single chapter). Anders confronts Theo privately: he knows who Theo is, and if Theo testifies, Margit will ruin Paloma financially through hidden liens. Anders offers Theo money to disappear again. Beat: corruption tightening its grip.

chapters.title: The Empty Workshop
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. Theo vanishes overnight, leaving tools behind and a note that says only 'I'm sorry. Ask Henrik.' Paloma, betrayed-feeling, finds Henrik's address and drives through the night. Beat: heartbreak converted into resolve.

chapters.title: Henrik's Room
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. Dying Henrik tells Paloma the whole truth: the fire, Anders, Margit's cover-up, and that the boy she loved took the blame's shadow and ran to protect her. Paloma realizes Theo's fake date was a homecoming. Beat: grief and love reconciled.

chapters.title: The Hearing
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. At the county courthouse, Theo delivers the rehearsed sentence at last: 'I saw Anders Eriksen start the fire, and I stayed silent for ten years.' Margit's lawyer dismantles his credibility; Anders watches coldly. Beat: climax — truth spoken at maximum cost.

chapters.title: Everything Auctioned
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. With the scandal public, Margit withdraws the rescue offer and the bank accelerates the auction. Paloma stands in the empty tasting room, ready to lose everything — until Theo arrives with Henrik's signed affidavit and a buyer: himself, offering his savings as a partner, not a rescuer. Beat: love as equal terms.

chapters.title: The Vote of the Family
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Confronted by Paloma, Theo, and the affidavit, the family fractures: Anders confesses to their mother; Margit's control collapses. Anders, facing charges, asks Paloma not for forgiveness but for silence's opposite — the truth told fully. Beat: power undone by honesty.

chapters.title: First Harvest Together
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Months later: charges resolved, debts restructured, the two of them co-owning the Old Mill House. During the first harvest, Theo finally kisses her properly among the vines, finishing every sentence the fire interrupted. Beat: tenderness earned.

chapters.title: The Summer Keeps Its Word
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. Epilogue at the restored mill, one year on: a small festival, Henrik's chair empty but honored, Paloma writing new numbers in the ledger — this time in ink, not pencil. She keeps love in the present tense now. Beat: peace, memory redeemed, future open.
